items.text: Keep the house with its ancestral shrine intact from generation to generation; never divide it.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂 總 立廟世數
items.quote: 凡祠堂所在之宅，宗子，世守之，不得分析。 — The house where the ancestral shrine is located, the lineage heir shall keep it in perpetuity and not divide it.

items.text: When building a house, build the ancestral shrine first.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂 總 立廟世數
items.quote: 君子，將營宮室，宗廟爲先。 — A nobleman, when about to build a dwelling, places the ancestral shrine first.

items.text: Do not set up a separate lineage temple: bring offerings to the temple at the lineage heir's house.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂 總 立廟世數
items.quote: 宗子爲士，立二廟，支子爲大夫，當立三廟。然不可異宗別統。故其廟，亦立於宗子之家。 — If the lineage heir is a common officer and a branch son is a high minister, the branch son may have three temples, but he must not split the lineage; his temple is also erected at the lineage heir's house.

items.text: Hold a heart that repays origins and honors ancestors.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂 總 立廟世數
items.quote: 報本反始之心，尊祖敬宗之意。 — The heart that repays the root and returns to the beginning, the intention to honor ancestors and revere the lineage.

heading: 常變通攷 卷一 · 祠堂 · 祠堂 · 前後室並配 … 立廟疑變

items.text: When you offer the ancestral sacrifices, enshrine both your father's first wife and later wife together, because both were formally married.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Shrine: 前後室並配 … 立廟疑變
items.quote: 朱子曰：『繼室，亦禮聘，當並配。』— Zhu Xi said, 'A later wife was also formally married, so she should be enshrined together.'

items.text: Place your father's tablet on the west (right) and your mother's on the east (left) in the shrine, for the spirit way honors the right.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Shrine: 前後室並配 … 立廟疑變
items.quote: 今祭禮，考妣同席南向，則考西妣東，自合禮意。— In current rites, when father and mother share a mat facing south, father on the west and mother on the east fits the ritual meaning.

items.text: When you travel far to serve in office, carry the ancestral tablets with you and set up a temporary shrine so that the sacrifices are not interrupted.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Shrine: 前後室並配 … 立廟疑變
items.quote: 主祭者，出仕，卽告廟，以櫝，載位版，而行於官所，權立祠堂以祭之。— When the primary officiant goes out to office, he should report to the shrine, carry the tablets in a case, and at his post set up a temporary shrine to offer sacrifices.

items.text: As a son who is not the lineage heir, do not take the ancestral tablets with you to your post; that right belongs only to the heir.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Shrine: 前後室並配 … 立廟疑變
items.quote: 今人支子，爲守宰，奉神主以行，何如？答，此，非禮之正，亦亂後權宜之道也。— Nowadays, a non-heir son who becomes a governor takes the spirit tablets with him; answer: this is not proper ritual, but a wartime expedient.

items.text: While your father lives and leads the ancestral sacrifices, do not establish your own separate shrine when you are away in office.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Shrine: 前後室並配 … 立廟疑變
items.quote: 父在主祭，子出仕宦，不得祭。— When father is alive and primary officiant, a son who goes out to office may not sacrifice separately.

items.text: As the legitimate heir, you bear the responsibility to establish and preserve the ancestral shrine and perform the sacrifices.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Shrine: 前後室並配 … 立廟疑變
items.quote: 嫡統，承重立廟，羣弟，雖並爲諸侯，未得立廟。— The legitimate heir, bearing the heavy responsibility, establishes the shrine; the younger brothers, even if all lords, may not establish separate shrines.

items.text: If you are a son of a concubine and achieve high office, offer your sacrifices at the house of the lineage heir, not in your own separate shrine.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Shrine: 前後室並配 … 立廟疑變
items.quote: 庶子爲大夫，以上牲，祭於宗子之家— A son of a concubine who becomes a high official, with a higher-grade animal, sacrifices at the house of the lineage heir.
