items.text: Arrange the spirit tablets in the shrine in order: the high ancestor in the west, then great-grandfather, grandfather, father, each in his own niche, all facing south.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 常變通攷 卷一 · 祠堂 · 祠堂 · 昭穆 … 考妣合櫝
items.quote: 高祖居西，曾祖次之，祖次之，父次之 — High ancestor in the west, great-grandfather next, grandfather next, father next.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration: giving offerings to the dead is contrary to worship of God alone (Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20).

items.text: Keep the zhao and mu lines fixed: fathers are always on the zhao side, sons on the mu side, in every generation; do not move or reverse them.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 常變通攷 卷一 · 祠堂 · 祠堂 · 昭穆 … 考妣合櫝
items.quote: 昭常爲昭，穆常爲穆 — Zhao is always zhao, mu is always mu.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration: giving offerings to the dead is contrary to worship of God alone (Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20).

items.text: Sacrifice to ancestors up to the fourth generation because you wear mourning for them, even if the state code restricts you to two or three generations; do not create or destroy tablets based on official rank.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 常變通攷 卷一 · 祠堂 · 祠堂 · 昭穆 … 考妣合櫝
items.quote: 高祖有服，不可不祭 — The great-great-grandfather has mourning relations, so he cannot be left unsacrificed.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration: giving offerings to the dead is contrary to worship of God alone (Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20).

items.text: When offering sacrifice, use the spirit tablet, not a portrait; if the portrait differs in a single hair, it would be another person you are sacrificing to.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 常變通攷 卷一 · 祠堂 · 祠堂 · 昭穆 … 考妣合櫝
items.quote: 一髭髮，不相似，則所祭，已是別人 — If a single hair is not similar, then the one sacrificed to is already another person.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration itself is idolatrous; images are forbidden (Exod 20:4-5; 1 Cor 10:14).

items.text: As a filial son or grandson, follow the family rites and sacrifice to four generations, not merely the two or three that the state code allows, and do not let your rank determine which ancestors you honor.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 常變通攷 卷一 · 祠堂 · 祠堂 · 昭穆 … 考妣合櫝
items.quote: 孝子慈孫，依禮斷然行之，則豈有不可？ — Filial sons and loving grandsons, if they resolutely follow the rites, how could it be not permissible?
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration: giving offerings to the dead is contrary to worship of God alone (Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20).

items.text: When you have a great matter in the family, report it to the ruler and then offer the great joint sacrifice that includes your high ancestor.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 常變通攷 卷一 · 祠堂 · 祠堂 · 昭穆 … 考妣合櫝
items.quote: 大夫有事，省於其君，干祫及其高祖 — When a great officer has a matter, he reports to his lord and then the great joint sacrifice reaches his high ancestor.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration: giving offerings to the dead is contrary to worship of God alone (Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20).

items.text: Place the father's and mother's tablets together in one box, each tablet separate, so husband and wife share the same receptacle.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 常變通攷 卷一 · 祠堂 · 祠堂 · 昭穆 … 考妣合櫝
items.quote: 府君夫人，共爲一櫝 — Husband and wife share one box.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration: giving offerings to the dead is contrary to worship of God alone (Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20).

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷一 · 宗法 · 宗法 · 總論 … 立子立孫之辨

items.text: Revere the lineage heir as the one who presides over the ancestors and unites the clan.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 宗者，尊也，爲先祖主也，宗人之所尊也。

items.text: Preside over the ancestral sacrifices as the household's chief officiant.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 宗子承家主祭，有君之道。
items.conflict: Ancestral offerings conflict with the first commandment; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: Do not offer sacrifices on your own; when you must offer, first tell the lineage heir.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 支子不祭，祭必告於宗子。
items.conflict: Ancestral offerings conflict with the first commandment; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: If the lineage heir lives in another country, make an altar facing the grave and offer.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 宗子居于他國，則庶子望墓爲壇以祭。
items.conflict: Ancestral offerings conflict with the first commandment; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: Unite and govern the clan, sharing resources and resolving needs.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 大宗能率小宗，小宗能率羣弟，通其有無，所以統理族人者也。

items.text: Submit to the order of elder and younger: younger generation follows the older.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 古者，子弟從父兄，今父兄從子弟，由不知本也。

items.text: Discipline children who neglect the family shrine or ancestral duties.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 子弟不奉家廟...幷行夏楚。

items.text: At seventy, hand over the management of family affairs to your son or grandson.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 七十曰老而傳。

items.text: When transferring the headship, announce it at the ancestral shrine.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 傳重告廟之文，只言傳重而已。
items.conflict: Ancestral offerings conflict with the first commandment; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: When the eldest son is dead, establish his eldest son as heir, not a younger son.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 孔子曰：否，立孫。

items.text: Provide betrothal gifts and dowries for clan members when they marry.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 娶婦嫁女，給聘奩物。

items.text: Help one another in weddings, condolences, and funerals.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites 1: Zongfa Zonglun, Lizi Lisun zhi Bian
items.quote: 賓客慶弔送終。

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷二 · 深衣制度 · 深衣制度 · 圓袂 … 黑緣

items.text: When both parents are living, edge the deep garment with blue; when both parents and grandparents are living, edge it with patterned silk, to show reverence.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 2
items.quote: 具父母大父母，衣純以繪；具父母，衣純以靑 — If both parents and grandparents are alive, edge with patterned silk; if only parents, edge with blue.

items.text: If your father is dead, edge the deep garment with plain white to express mourning for him.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 2
items.quote: 如孤子，衣純以素 — If orphan, edge with plain white.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷一 · 祠堂 · 祠堂 · 遺書衣物 … 易世則改題遞遷

items.text: Set aside a twentieth of each household's field as sacrificial land, manage it as the lineage heir, and never sell or pawn it; use its yield only for offerings.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Ancestral Shrine
items.quote: 宗子，主之，以給祭用...不得典賣 — The heir manages it to supply sacrifices... must not sell or pawn.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the worship of God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Keep sacrificial vessels stored apart and never use them for common purposes; even in poverty, do not sell them; when worn out, bury or burn them rather than let them be defiled.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Ancestral Shrine
items.quote: 皆具貯於庫中，而封鎖之，不得他用...君子雖貧，不粥祭器 — Store them in a locked storehouse and do not use them for other purposes... a noble man, though poor, does not sell sacrificial vessels.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the worship of God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Preserve the garments left by ancestors; store them in the shrine and bring them out only to clothe the personator at sacrifices.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Ancestral Shrine
items.quote: 遺衣服，藏焉，若將祭祀，則各以其服，授尸 — Store the left-behind clothes; when about to sacrifice, bring out each garment to give to the personator.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the worship of God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: If you are the son of a concubine and inherit the family rites, sacrifice to your own mother only in a private room, and only during your own lifetime; do not pass it to your descendants.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Ancestral Shrine
items.quote: 妾子承重者，祭其母於私室，止其身 — A concubine's son who inherits sacrifices to his mother in a private room, and only during his own lifetime.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the worship of God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: For a collateral relative who died without an heir, attach the tablet to the proper ancestor; if there is no proper place, sacrifice in a separate room.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Ancestral Shrine
items.quote: 從宜而祀之別室，其亦可也 — It is also permissible to sacrifice to them in a separate room as appropriate.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the worship of God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: If the great-grandfather's tablet is due for burial but the great-grandmother still lives, do not bury it yet; keep it in a separate room to spare her grief.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Ancestral Shrine
items.quote: 高祖母在，則情理不忍...奉安別室，恐當 — If great-grandmother is alive, it is unbearable to bury it; place it in a separate room, I think.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷二 · 參 · 參 · 正至朔朢則參 … 國恤中朔參

items.text: Lead the household in the regular shrine visits on New Year, winter solstice, and the first and fifteenth of each month; open the tablets, offer incense and libation, and bow.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, vol. 2, '參' chapter (正至朔朢則參 國恤中朔參)
items.quote: 主人以下盛服，入門就位...主人詣香卓前降神。搢笏焚香再拜...酹于茅上...再拜參神。 — The master and all below, in full dress, enter and take their places... The master goes before the incense table to call down the spirits; he inserts the tablet into his girdle, burns incense and bows twice... he pours a libation on the grass... bows twice to greet the spirits.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the first commandment; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: Assist your husband in the shrine rite by taking out the tablets of the female ancestors and placing them east of the male tablets; then stand with him and bow.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, vol. 2, '參' chapter (正至朔朢則參 國恤中朔參)
items.quote: 主婦盥帨升，奉諸妣神主，置于考東。 — The mistress washes and dries her hands, ascends, and takes out the tablets of the foremothers, placing them east of the forefathers.
items.conflict: Same as above; ancestor veneration is not commanded for Christians.

items.text: When your husband is dead, yield the direction of the family rites to your son and his wife; do not act as mistress, but take the place of honor before her.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, vol. 2, '參' chapter (正至朔朢則參 國恤中朔參)
items.quote: 舅沒則姑老，不預於祭...故今專以世適宗子夫婦，爲主人主婦...其有母...則設特位於前如此。 — When the father-in-law is gone, the mother-in-law retires and does not take part in the sacrifice... Therefore now only the direct-line heir and his wife act as master and mistress; if there is a mother, she is given a special place in front.

items.text: Assist your father in the shrine rites; when he orders, take out the tablets of the lesser ancestors; if he is unable to attend, perform the rite in his place.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, vol. 2, '參' chapter (正至朔朢則參 國恤中朔參)
items.quote: 命長子長婦或長女，盥帨升，分出諸祔主之卑者...有故而使子弟，猶或可也，婢僕必不可也。 — He orders the eldest son, eldest son's wife, or eldest daughter to wash and ascend, and separately take out the tablets of the lesser attached ancestors... If he has an excuse he may send his sons or younger brothers, but never servants.

items.text: If your father the heir cannot attend the regular shrine rite, go in his place; never allow a servant to perform it.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, vol. 2, '參' chapter (正至朔朢則參 國恤中朔參)
items.quote: 有故而使子弟，猶或可也，婢僕必不可也。 — If he has an excuse he may send his sons or younger brothers, but never servants.

items.text: Come to the shrine in your ceremonial clothes and take your assigned place; bow together with the master at the appointed times.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, vol. 2, '參' chapter (正至朔朢則參 國恤中朔參)
items.quote: 主人以下盛服，入門就位...與在位者，皆再拜參神。 — The master and those below, in full dress, enter and take their places... all who are present bow twice to greet the spirits.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with exclusive worship of God.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷二 · 俗節 · 俗節 · 俗節則獻以時食 … 薦新前遇新物

items.text: On seasonal festivals, offer the seasonal foods to the ancestors at the family shrine.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 2.俗節
items.quote: 凡鄕俗所尙者...薦以大盤 — On all that the local custom honors, present them in a large tray.
items.conflict: Deut. 18:10-12; offerings to the dead are idolatry

items.text: Do not eat new food before offering it to the ancestors.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 2.俗節
items.quote: 未嘗則人子不忍前食新也 — If he has not offered them, a son cannot bear to eat the new food beforehand.
items.conflict: Deut. 18:10-12; offerings to the dead are idolatry

items.text: If official duties prevent the New Year's rite on the day, perform it a few days before or after so as not to omit it.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 2.俗節
items.quote: 元朝則在官者有朝謁之禮...止於除夕前三四日行事 — On New Year's Day an official has the court audience; so perform it three or four days before New Year's Eve.
items.conflict: Deut. 18:10-12; offerings to the dead are idolatry

items.text: If the main lineage house cannot perform the seasonal rite, branch families should still perform it unless the main house is in great mourning.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 2.俗節
items.quote: 大宗雖有故不行，而小宗從而並廢，似未安 — If the great lineage has a reason not to perform, for the small lineage to follow and abolish it altogether seems uneasy.
items.conflict: Deut. 18:10-12; offerings to the dead are idolatry

items.text: After a burial in the household, have a family member in light mourning perform the offerings; before burial they are suspended.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 2.俗節
items.quote: 未葬可廢，旣葬則使輕服或已除者，行禮可也 — Before burial they may be suspended; after burial have one in light mourning or already out of mourning perform the rite.
items.conflict: Deut. 18:10-12; offerings to the dead are idolatry

items.text: Do not suspend ancestral rites because of mourning for a maternal or wife-side relative.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 2.俗節
items.quote: 死者於所祭無服則祭...今以舅喪不行節祀，似非禮意 — If the dead is one for whom the ancestors have no mourning, sacrifice; now to stop festival offerings because of an uncle's mourning seems not the meaning of the rites.
items.conflict: Deut. 18:10-12; offerings to the dead are idolatry

items.text: Offer new foods whenever they appear, not only on fixed days.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 2.俗節
items.quote: 但有新卽薦 — Whenever there is something new, offer it.
items.conflict: Deut. 18:10-12; offerings to the dead are idolatry

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷四 · 居家雜儀下 · 居家雜儀下 · 宮室之制

items.text: Place the ancestral shrine east of the main dwelling as the rites require.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 宮室之制
items.quote: 廟在寢東 — The ancestral shrine is east of the bedchamber.
items.conflict: Reformed Christians reject ancestor veneration; worship belongs to God alone (Ex. 20:3-5).

items.text: Seat the elder in the place of honor between the door and the window.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 宮室之制
items.quote: 戶西者尊處，以尊者及賓客，位于此 — The west side of the door is the honored place, for the honorable and guests.

items.text: Enter and leave by the side gate, not the main gate.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 宮室之制
items.quote: 婦人由闈門 — Women go by the side gate.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷一 · 宗法 · 宗法 · 立後 … 立後後生子

items.text: Do not agree to be adopted as heir by another family without your father's express command; to call your own parents uncle or brother without his order is to love gain more than kin.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 不承父命，而輒稱己父母爲伯叔，可乎？是貪利而忘親也。 — Not obeying father's command and calling one's own parents uncle or brother: that is loving gain and forgetting kin.

items.text: When your father commands you to be adopted as heir, obey his repeated command, even with tears, and go as he directs.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 父三命曰... 汝其敬承先命以往。 — Father commanded three times... You should respectfully receive the late command and go.

items.text: Serve your adoptive father and mother with filial care and respect; be diligent in your conduct and do not bring them anxiety or shame.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 善事嗣父嗣母，致養致敬，愼厥身修，毋貽憂辱。 — Serve well the adoptive father and mother, give nurture and respect, be careful in self-cultivation, do not cause worry or disgrace.

items.text: As adopted heir, continue the ancestral sacrifices of your adoptive line and see that its succession does not perish.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 往繼宗祀 — go to continue the ancestral sacrifices.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the second commandment and biblical teaching that the dead are not to be worshiped.

items.text: Love and instruct the children born later to your adoptive father; distribute the common property to them fairly and live with them in brotherly peace.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 爾其愛護敎導，均授常産，克友克養。 — You should love, care, teach, equally give the regular property, be brotherly and supportive.

items.text: Regard your adopted son as your true son, with no difference from a child of your own body; give him the full standing of a son.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 爲人後者，父子之倫，已定。與親子，無毫髮之殊。 — For one who becomes another's heir, the relation of father and son is fixed; with a natural son there is not a hair's difference.

items.text: Do not let the main line become extinct; appoint a branch son as its heir, preferring a younger son over the eldest legitimate son of a branch.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 大宗者，收族者也，不可以絶。故族人，以支子後大宗也。 — The great lineage gathers the clan and must not be cut off; therefore the clan uses a branch son to continue it.

items.text: If you are the only son and your father is dead, do not agree to be adopted out, lest your own father be left without a successor to his sacrifices.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 孤子不可出繼... 置其父於無後耳。 — An orphan son must not be adopted out... it places his father in the position of having no heir.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the second commandment and biblical teaching that the dead are not to be worshiped.

items.text: When you adopt an heir, report it at the ancestral shrine to the forebears; do not undertake such a change without informing them.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 詣祠堂，焚香再拜，跪告曰... 立以爲嗣，敢告。 — Go to the shrine, burn incense, bow twice, kneel and report... set him up as heir, daring to announce.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the second commandment and biblical teaching that the dead are not to be worshiped.

items.text: If you later beget a son of your own, divide the family property equally between him and the son you adopted first.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 立嗣之後，却生親子，其家産，幷許與元立均分。 — After establishing an heir, if you later beget a natural son, the family property is to be equally divided with the original heir.

items.text: Before giving your son as heir, command him to serve his adoptive father and mother with filial care and respect, and to love and share fairly with any later siblings.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 善事嗣父嗣母... 均授常産... — Serve well the adoptive parents... equally give the regular property...

items.text: When your son is adopted out, go to your own ancestral shrine and announce it to your forefathers.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 立後後生子
items.quote: 主人主婦帥子，詣祠堂，跪告曰... 今日出繼... 謹告。 — The master and his wife lead the son to the shrine, kneel and report... going out to be an heir... respectfully announce.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the second commandment and biblical teaching that the dead are not to be worshiped.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷一 · 不遷位 · 不遷位 · 不遷位 … 遠代不遷位屬稱

items.text: Honor the cadet-line founder as your lineage's first ancestor, and continue his cult through the generations without removal.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 別子爲祖，繼別爲宗，百世不遷之宗。 — The cadet-line founder becomes the ancestor; the one continuing him becomes the lineage head; there is a lineage head who is not removed for a hundred generations.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5 forbids honoring any but God; ancestor cult is idolatry.

items.text: When the founder's kinship distance is exhausted, store his tablet at the grave site, maintain the grave field, and lead the kin in an annual grave rite forever.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 大宗之家，始祖親盡，則藏其主於墓所，而大宗猶主其墓田，以奉其墓祭，歲率宗人，一祭之，百世不改。 — In the house of the great lineage, when the founder's kinship distance is exhausted, his tablet is stored at the grave; the great lineage head still manages the grave land to offer the grave sacrifice, annually leading the kin to sacrifice once, never changing for a hundred generations.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; Deut 18:10-12 forbid rites for the dead.

items.text: If an ancestor was the first meritorious official and thus unremovable, set up a separate niche and offer sacrifices to him even beyond the standard generations.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 若有親盡之祖，始爲功臣而百世不遷者，則代數（三代）。外，別立一龕，祭之。 — If there is an ancestor whose kinship distance is exhausted but who was the first meritorious official and not removed for a hundred generations, then outside the standard generations, set up a separate niche and sacrifice to him.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; ancestor sacrifice is abomination.

items.text: Do not set up a separate shrine for ancestors who are not qualified (not a cadet-line founder or meritorious official), lest you overstep your station.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 若非諸侯別子與勳勞有君號者，則決不可別廟奉祀，以犯僭逼之嫌。 — Unless he is a cadet-line founder of a feudal lord or has meritorious service with a lord's title, you must not set up a separate shrine and offer sacrifices, so as not to commit the offense of usurpation.
items.conflict: This rule guards against idolatrous excess, but still presupposes ancestor veneration; cf. Ex 20:3.

items.text: When an unremovable ancestor occupies the shrine, move the fourth-generation ancestor's tablet to a separate room to keep within the allowed number of generations.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 不遷之位，四代祖雖未代盡，而出安別室耳。 — The unmovable tablet: even though the fourth-generation ancestor's turn has not fully come, he is moved out and placed in a separate room.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; any ancestor rite is forbidden.

items.text: Do not set up an unremovable tablet as a fifth niche, for that would be usurping a lord's prerogative.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 四龕外，又特設，則乃五龕也，僭不可爲也。 — Beyond the four niches, to set up another special one would be a fifth niche; it is usurpation and must not be done.
items.conflict: The prohibition itself reflects the first commandment's exclusive worship, but the system of ancestor niches is unscriptural.

items.text: Only the first meritorious official is unremovable; move the tablets of later meritorious ancestors after their prescribed generations.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 《大典》，只言『始爲功臣。』則第二以下，祧遷，從可知也。 — The Great Code only says 'the first meritorious official'; so the second and later ones are moved, as can be known from this.
items.conflict: Ancestor cult is forbidden; see Deut 18:11.

items.text: When the founder's tablet is stored at the grave site, cease the regular shrine rites and offer only the annual grave rite.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 神主旣藏於墓所，則時祭忌祭，當準禮廢之。楊氏曰，『有祠堂以奉墓祭。』 — Once the spirit tablet is stored at the grave, the seasonal and death-day sacrifices should be discontinued according to ritual; Yang says, 'There is a shrine hall to offer the grave sacrifice.'
items.conflict: All rites to the dead are prohibited; Isaiah 8:19.
items.needs_role: founder whose tablet is at the grave

items.text: Set up a separate shrine for the unremovable ancestor and maintain it to unify and oversee the clan.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 且依《家禮》，別立廟，使宗子主之，庶幾維持管攝，爲收宗族厚風俗之一事。 — Moreover, according to the Family Rituals, set up a separate shrine, let the lineage heir preside over it, and thereby hope to maintain and govern, as one matter of gathering the clan and enriching customs.
items.conflict: Using ancestor worship to unify the clan replaces God's order with idolatry; see Col 2:18.

items.text: Address the unremovable ancestor as 'forefather' or 'Nth-generation ancestor', not 'first ancestor', to avoid presumption toward the first ancestor of all people.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 問，「或書幾代祖，或書始祖。」答，「稱先祖，可也，或稱幾代祖，亦可也。始祖之稱，似有嫌於厥初生民之祖，恐未安。」 — Question: 'Some write Nth-generation ancestor, some write first ancestor.' Answer: 'Calling him forefather is acceptable, or Nth-generation ancestor is also acceptable. The title first ancestor seems to be suspected of referring to the first ancestor of all people, which is uncomfortable.'
items.conflict: Honoring ancestors with cultic titles is part of ancestor worship; see 1 Tim 2:5.

items.text: If an ancestor was not a meritorious official, even if he is honored in a shrine or academy, his tablet must be moved when his generations are exhausted.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo 1, Bulcheonwi
items.quote: 國法，始爲功臣者，爲不遷之位，非功臣，則雖享於祠院，不可不遷於廟也。 — By state law, the first meritorious official becomes an unremovable position; if not a meritorious official, even if he is honored in a shrine or academy, he must not fail to be moved to the main shrine.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the first commandment (Ex 20:3).

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷四 · 居家雜儀下 · 居家雜儀下 · 親屬

items.text: Be close to kin: love them while they live and mourn them when they die, gathering for their joys and sorrows.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 親屬
items.quote: 上湊高祖，下至玄孫。一家有吉，百家聚之，生相親愛，死相哀痛 — From high ancestor to distant descendant, when one family has joy, a hundred families gather; in life they love, in death they mourn.

items.text: Call those who have adopted you as heir your father and mother, not as uncle or aunt.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 親屬
items.quote: 旣是爲人後者，便須將所後者，呼之以爲父，以爲母 — One who is made another's heir must call the one he succeeds father and mother.

items.text: Count your natural parents as uncle and aunt once you are adopted out as heir; do not call them father and mother.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 親屬
items.quote: 本父母，反呼之以爲叔爲伯也 — Your original parents are to be called uncle and aunt instead.

items.text: Treat your natural brothers and sisters as cousins after adoption, not as siblings.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 親屬
items.quote: 旣稱伯叔父母，則稱從弟，正合程朱之論 — If they are called uncle and aunt, then call them cousin; this agrees with Cheng and Zhu.

items.text: Give your father's legal wife the respect due a mother; before her use the title a servant uses for the mistress.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 親屬
items.quote: 妾子之於嫡母，稱於人則曰嫡母可也。但以方言，稱於母前及家內，則別無可當之稱。恐只得如今人家婢御稱主母之辭而已 — A concubine's son may call his father's legal wife 'legal mother' to others, but before her and at home he must use only the term a servant uses for the mistress.

items.text: Do not take a second principal wife while the first lives, for having two equal wives is a grave breach of propriety.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 親屬
items.quote: 並后匹嫡，禮之大忌 — Side-by-side queens and equal wives are a great taboo of propriety.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷二 · 祠堂禍變 · 祠堂禍變 · 有水火盜賊先救祠堂 … 避亂埋主之節

items.text: In flight or disaster, first rescue the spirit tablets and ancestral writings, then the ritual vessels, and only afterward the household goods.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂禍變: 有水火盜賊先救祠堂…避亂埋主之節
items.quote: 遷神主遺書，次及祭器。然後及家財。 — First move the spirit tablets and inherited writings, then the sacrificial vessels, and only then the household goods.

items.text: When the shrine is damaged by fire or collapse, move the tablets to safety, repair the shrine, and offer wine and fruit to inform and comfort the spirits.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂禍變: 有水火盜賊先救祠堂…避亂埋主之節
items.quote: 謹以酒果，用伸虔告。 — With wine and fruit, we reverently inform and comfort the spirits.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the exclusive worship of God (Exod 20:3–5).

items.text: When the ancestral shrine burns, weep for three days and wear plain clothes as mourning.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂禍變: 有水火盜賊先救祠堂…避亂埋主之節
items.quote: 有焚其先人之室，則三日哭。 — If one's ancestor's shrine is burned, weep for three days.
items.conflict: Prescribed mourning for a shrine is a rite for the dead, forbidden (Deut 18:11).

items.text: When spirit tablets are burned, set up a temporary seat at the former shrine, burn incense, call back the scattered spirit, remake the tablets, and perform a comfort rite in plain clothes.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂禍變: 有水火盜賊先救祠堂…避亂埋主之節
items.quote: 設虛位，改題神主，焚香設祭，使飄散之神，更依於神主可也。 — Set up an empty seat, remake the tablet, burn incense, and offer sacrifice so the scattered spirit may again reside in the tablet.
items.conflict: Necromancy and rites for the dead are forbidden (Deut 18:10–12).

items.text: If remaking tablets during a mourning period, inscribe the name of the principal mourner and have the nearest relative make the announcement.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂禍變: 有水火盜賊先救祠堂…避亂埋主之節
items.quote: 以喪人題主，則主祝代告，以族中最親者一人，措辭以告。 — When inscribing with the mourner's name, have the closest relative make the announcement.
items.conflict: Naming on ancestral tablets is part of ancestor veneration (Exod 20:4).

items.text: When remaking tablets after a fire, transfer the tablets of ancestors beyond five generations to the eldest branch of the clan; do not keep them in the main house.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂禍變: 有水火盜賊先救祠堂…避亂埋主之節
items.quote: 今以親盡，祧遷于叔父某之家。 — Now that the relation has ended, transfer the tablet to the uncle's house.

items.text: Do not remake spirit tablets for ancestors whose generations have already passed; their tablets should have been buried.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂禍變: 有水火盜賊先救祠堂…避亂埋主之節
items.quote: 追造於親盡之後，恐未合禮。 — To remake after the relation has ended is not in accord with ritual.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the exclusive worship of God (Exod 20:3–5).

items.text: In wartime or flight, bury the spirit tablets behind the shrine rather than carry them; do so openly, and family members should bow and weep.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 祠堂禍變: 有水火盜賊先救祠堂…避亂埋主之節
items.quote: 毋寧埋安於祠堂之後？幸而生還，則可以依舊奉安矣。 — Rather bury them behind the shrine; if you survive, you can enshrine them again.
items.conflict: Bowing to tablets is a form of ancestor worship, forbidden (Exod 20:5).

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷二 · 有事則告 · 有事則告 · 告辭 … 所告之辭少則不用祝

items.text: When you receive a posthumous title for your parent, go to the shrine, offer food and drink, burn the edict, and report it with grief and gratitude.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 有事則告 告辭
items.quote: 祿不及養，摧咽難勝 — The salary comes too late to support them; grief is hard to bear.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with biblical teaching; God alone is to be worshiped (Exod 20:3-5; Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Report to your deceased wife when she receives a posthumous title or when her title is changed; offer and announce it to her spirit.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 有事則告 告辭
items.quote: 奉奠致詔，君其聽之。尙饗 — I present the offering and edict; listen, and receive.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead conflict with biblical teaching; the dead cannot hear or receive gifts (Eccl 9:5; Luke 16:19-31).

items.text: Present your newborn son at the ancestral shrine and announce his birth to the ancestors.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 有事則告 告辭
items.quote: 某之婦某氏，以某月某日，生子名某，敢見 — My wife gave birth on a certain date; I dare to present the child.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with biblical worship; God alone is to be honored (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: When you adopt an heir, lead him to the ancestral shrine and announce the adoption so the lineage continues.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 有事則告 告辭
items.quote: 過房與之，更名立爲嗣子，尙冀先靈陰隲 — Adopt him, rename him as heir, hope the ancestors bless.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with biblical teaching; the dead cannot bless or intervene (Deut 18:10-12; Heb 9:27).

items.text: When you move to a new house, report at the ancestral shrine to settle the ancestors' spirits there.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 有事則告 告辭
items.quote: 今旣定宅，敢伸虔告，以安祖考之靈 — Now the house is set; I report to settle the ancestors' spirits.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with biblical teaching; the dead have no power over places (Eccl 9:5-6; Luke 16:19-31).

items.text: When you pass the civil exam or receive an official post, report at the ancestral shrine and thank the ancestors.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 有事則告 告辭
items.quote: 蒙恩授某科某第及第，奉承先訓，獲忝出身 — By grace received degree; following ancestral teaching, obtained rank.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with biblical teaching; success is from God alone, not ancestors (Deut 8:17-18; Jas 1:17).

items.text: If your parent's body is not found, report at the shrine and ask the ancestors to help find it; if after three years still missing, report again.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 有事則告 告辭
items.quote: 亡其親，必告其先廟，使咸知之。求三年，若不得也，則又告之 — If parent is missing, report to shrine; if not found in three years, report again.
items.conflict: Seeking help from the dead conflicts with biblical teaching; the dead cannot assist the living (Deut 18:10-12; Isa 8:19).

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷二 · 晨謁 · 晨謁 · 主人晨謁於大門之內 … 出入必告

items.text: Each morning at the family shrine, burn incense and bow twice to the ancestors.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 晨謁
items.quote: 深衣焚香再拜 — In deep robes, burn incense and bow twice.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the first commandment: worship God alone (Exod 20:3-5); do not inquire of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: When ascending or descending at the shrine, only the lineage heir uses the east steps; all others, even elders, use the west steps.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 晨謁
items.quote: 凡升降，惟主人由阼階，主婦及餘人，雖尊長亦由西階。 — In all ascending and descending, only the head uses the east steps; the wife and others, even elders, use the west steps.

items.text: When the head leads morning worship, follow his lead: line up, bow in order, light incense, and bow again before withdrawing.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 晨謁
items.quote: 先生陞堂率子弟，以次列拜，炷香又拜而退。 — The master ascended the hall leading the sons and younger brothers; they bowed in order, lit incense, bowed again, and withdrew.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the first commandment: worship God alone (Exod 20:3-5); do not inquire of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Do not conduct the morning audience alone when the head is absent; if you must, perform it outside the gate to avoid his place.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 晨謁
items.quote: 無主人則不許獨行，固是嚴宗法之意... 行於大門之外，以避主人之位如何？ — Without the head, do not perform it alone; the intention is to honor the lineage law... perform it outside the gate to avoid the head's place.

items.text: While mourning a parent, suspend the morning audience for three years.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 喪中廢晨謁
items.quote: 三年之內，姑闕之耶？... 當姑闕 — Should it be omitted during the three years? ... It should be omitted.

items.text: As acting head, perform the morning audience in place of the lineage heir.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 攝主晨謁
items.quote: 旣云攝主，宜攝此禮。 — Since you are acting head, you should carry out this rite.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the first commandment: worship God alone (Exod 20:3-5); do not inquire of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Avoid using the east steps; use the west steps to respect the absent head's place.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 攝主晨謁
items.quote: 主人由阼階，則攝主亦當由阼階否？曰：恐當避。 — If the head uses the east steps, should the acting head also use them? Answer: I fear he should avoid them.

items.text: The lineage heir, with his wife, before going out and upon returning, bow and announce your departure and return to the ancestors; for longer absences, add incense and more bows.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 出入必告
items.quote: 遠出經旬以上，則再拜焚香告云：「某將適某所敢告。」 — For a long journey of more than ten days, bow twice, burn incense, and announce: 'Your servant will go to such-and-such place; I presume to announce.'
items.conflict: Conflicts with the first commandment: worship God alone (Exod 20:3-5); do not inquire of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Other family members also announce departures and returns to the ancestors, but do not open the middle gate.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 出入必告
items.quote: 餘人亦然，但不開中門。 — Others do the same, but do not open the middle gate.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the first commandment: worship God alone (Exod 20:3-5); do not inquire of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: In ancestor rites, the wife bows four times while the head bows twice.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law, 男子再拜婦人四拜
items.quote: 凡拜，男子再拜，則婦人四拜，謂之俠拜。 — In all bowing, men bow twice, women bow four times; this is called mutual bowing.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the first commandment: worship God alone (Exod 20:3-5); do not inquire of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷四 · 居家雜儀下 · 居家雜儀下 · 親屬

items.text: Serve your father's brothers as you serve your father.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 親屬
items.quote: 呼爲伯父叔父者，言事之之禮，與父同也。 — Calling them '伯父' and '叔父' is because the rites of serving them are the same as for one's father.

items.text: Give way to your father's concubine who acts as mistress of the household: in seating and eating, yield to her as to the acting mistress.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 親屬
items.quote: 宜坐則當避，食則當讓。 — In sitting, yield your seat; in eating, yield precedence.
items.conflict: Concubinage (secondary wife) is not biblical monogamy; a concubine has no legitimate authority as mistress.

items.text: Do not return the bow of your husband's concubine; maintain the distinction between wife and concubine.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 親屬
items.quote: 女君不報，則敬與婦同而又加賤也。 — The wife does not return the bow, for the concubine's respect is like that of a daughter-in-law to her mother-in-law, but her status is lower.
items.conflict: All persons are created equal in dignity; maintaining a class distinction between wife and concubine is not consistent with Christian teaching.

items.text: If you are a concubine and mother of the son performing ancestral rites, do not take the place of the legal wife; if she is absent, leave her place empty.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 親屬
items.quote: 嫡母在，則宜在母位，嫡母不在，則宜虛其位。 — If the legal mother is alive, she stands in the mother's place; if not, that place should be empty.
items.conflict: Ancestral rites are worship of the dead; concubinage is not biblical.
items.needs_role: father's concubine who is birth mother (妾子之母)

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷三 · 居家雜儀上 · 居家雜儀上 總

items.text: Greet your elders each morning and evening; rise when an elder passes, dismount when you meet an elder on the road, and bow the prescribed number of times.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 凡卑幼於尊長，晨亦省問，夜亦安置。坐而尊長過之則起

items.text: Do not talk casually or have private contact with your brother-in-law or sister-in-law.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 嫂叔不通問

items.text: When a married sister returns to the parental home, do not sit with her on the same mat or eat from the same dishes.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 姑姊妹女子子，已嫁而返，兄弟不與同席而坐，不與共器而食。

items.text: On New Year's Day and the first and fifteenth of each month, assemble in the hall and bow to the household head and elders in proper order.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 冬至朔朢，聚於堂上，共拜家長

items.text: At seasonal and family banquets, offer a cup of wine to the household head with a blessing, and bow before and after he drinks.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 上壽於家長...伏願某官，備膺五福，保族宜家

items.text: Train your children from infancy: teach them to use the right hand, to address elders respectfully, to read the classics, and to know right from wrong.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 子能食，飼之敎以右手，子能言，敎之自名及唱喏萬福安置

items.text: Teach your daughter to be gentle, obedient, and skilled in women's work; do not have her learn to compose poetry or play popular music.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 女子則敎以婉娩聽從及女工之大者

items.text: Before you are capped or pinned, rise early, wash your face, go to see your elders, assist them in serving food, and help at sacrificial rites.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 未冠笄者，質明而起，總角靧面，以見尊長

items.text: Rise at cockcrow, sweep the house, prepare toiletries, wait on your master and mistress, and do laundry and sewing for them before your own.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 凡內外僕妾，雞初鳴咸起...得間則浣濯紉縫，先公後私

items.text: Provide food and clothing for your servants; teach them before punishing, and dismiss those who are deceitful, thieving, or rebellious.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 婢僕，代我之勞，當先恩而後威...必須軫念飢寒，資給衣食

items.text: Bow to each other in mutual respect, as husband and wife.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 夫婦對拜

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷二 · 有事則告 · 有事則告 · 告廟之儀 … 三獻行祭之儀

items.text: When any matter occurs, report it to the ancestors by offering tea and wine, bowing twice, and having the written declaration read.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Yusa jeuk go 2
items.quote: 如正至朔日之儀。但獻茶酒再拜。 — As on the first day of the month, but offer tea and wine and bow twice.
items.conflict: The dead cannot hear; ancestor rites are forbidden (Deut 18:10-12; Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Use the proper self-designation according to your relation to the most senior ancestor; unless you are the lineage heir, do not say 'filial'.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Yusa jeuk go 2
items.quote: 凡自稱，非宗子，不言孝。 — In all self-designation, unless you are the lineage heir, do not say 'filial'.
items.conflict: The dead cannot hear; ancestor rites are forbidden (Deut 18:10-12; Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: When the matter concerns a descendant of a younger son, the lineage heir must also report it to the ancestors.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Yusa jeuk go 2
items.quote: 若介子孫之事，則主人亦告。 — If it concerns a younger son's descendant, the master also reports.
items.conflict: The dead cannot hear; ancestor rites are forbidden (Deut 18:10-12; Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: After the report is read, the person concerned must himself go between the two steps and bow twice to the ancestors.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Yusa jeuk go 2
items.quote: 告畢，當身進于兩階間再拜。 — After the report, the person concerned goes between the two steps and bows twice.
items.conflict: The dead cannot hear; ancestor rites are forbidden (Deut 18:10-12; Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: If there is no officiant to read the declaration, the lineage heir must read it himself.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Yusa jeuk go 2
items.quote: 無祝人則主人自讀。 — If there is no reader, the master reads it himself.
items.conflict: The dead cannot hear; ancestor rites are forbidden (Deut 18:10-12; Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: If you are demoted, report your failure and shame to the ancestors.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Yusa jeuk go 2
items.quote: 貶某官，荒墜先訓，皇恐無地。 — Demoted to such office, I have failed my ancestors' teaching; I am terrified and have nowhere to hide.
items.conflict: The dead cannot hear; ancestor rites are forbidden (Deut 18:10-12; Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: When a posthumous honor is conferred on an ancestor, report it, change the tablet inscription, and offer food and wine.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Yusa jeuk go 2
items.quote: 告追贈，則只告所贈之龕。 — When reporting a posthumous honor, report only to that ancestor's niche.
items.conflict: The dead cannot hear; ancestor rites are forbidden (Deut 18:10-12; Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: If you have a living father or elder brother, let him preside over the ancestral ceremony; stand in your own place and do not take the lead.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Yusa jeuk go 2
items.quote: 若仕者有父兄，則父兄主祭，仕者立本位。 — If the official has a father or elder brother, that senior presides; the official stands in his own place.
items.conflict: No one should lead ancestor rites; God alone is to be worshiped.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷四 · 居家雜儀下 · 居家雜儀下 · 拜跪之節

items.text: When meeting parents-in-law, perform a deep bow with hands touching the ground.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Baigui zhi jie
items.quote: 若見舅姑，則當扱地 — When meeting parents-in-law, you should touch the ground with your hands.

items.text: When meeting your mother-in-law, answer her single bow with two bows.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Baigui zhi jie
items.quote: 婿見婦之母，主婦一拜，婿答再拜，主婦又拜 — When the son-in-law sees the wife's mother, the wife's mother bows once, the son-in-law answers with two bows, the wife's mother bows again.

items.text: When acting as chief mourner for your husband, perform jisang (touching the forehead to the ground) instead of the hand bow.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Baigui zhi jie
items.quote: 為喪主則稽顙 — If you are the chief mourner, then do jisang.

items.text: When acting as chief mourner for your eldest son, perform jisang (touching the forehead to the ground) instead of the hand bow.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Baigui zhi jie
items.quote: 為喪主則稽顙 — If you are the chief mourner, then do jisang.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷一 · 宗法 · 宗法 · 次子之子承重與否 … 長孫無子而有弟叔父不當攝祀

items.text: Offer the ancestral rites as the legitimate heir; a son of a concubine must not take that place.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites, Lineage Law, 次子之子承重與否 … 長孫無子而有弟叔父不當攝祀
items.quote: 雖有妾産，恐未可遽代承也 — Even if there are children of a concubine, they cannot hastily take over.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the First Commandment (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Even if the eldest son is disabled, do not transfer the ancestral rites to a younger brother; if he has a son, the line continues through him.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites, Lineage Law, 次子之子承重與否 … 長孫無子而有弟叔父不當攝祀
items.quote: 長子雖病廢，似不可傳重於次子，况長子有子，則豈可以次子奉祀耶？ — Though the eldest son is ill or disabled, it seems one cannot transfer the heavy responsibility to the second son; moreover, if the eldest son has a son, how could the second son preside over the rites?
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the First Commandment (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: When no legitimate heir remains, let the eldest son's son by a concubine preside over the rites rather than the second son's.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites, Lineage Law, 次子之子承重與否 … 長孫無子而有弟叔父不當攝祀
items.quote: 次嫡又無嫡，則長子之庶，似可奉祀 — If the second legitimate son also has no legitimate son, then the concubine's son of the eldest son seems to be able to preside.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the First Commandment (Exod 20:3-5).
items.needs_role: illegitimate son of the eldest son

items.text: If you preside temporarily because the heir cannot, stand aside when he is grown or able; the rites are his.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites, Lineage Law, 次子之子承重與否 … 長孫無子而有弟叔父不當攝祀
items.quote: 異時，甲之長孫長成，却改正 — Later, when A's eldest grandson grows up, correct it.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the First Commandment (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: While no heir is adopted, preside temporarily as the youngest brother; do not leave the rites unattended.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites, Lineage Law, 次子之子承重與否 … 長孫無子而有弟叔父不當攝祀
items.quote: 未立後前，以季爲攝主 — Before an heir is adopted, let the youngest brother be the temporary presider.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the First Commandment (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Preside temporarily if your elder brother cannot; the uncle must not step in.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites, Lineage Law, 次子之子承重與否 … 長孫無子而有弟叔父不當攝祀
items.quote: 有叔父，又有一弟，則其弟當奉祀 — If there is an uncle and also a younger brother, then the younger brother should preside.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the First Commandment (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Return the headship to the son of the disabled heir when he is born; inform the ancestors at the shrine.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites, Lineage Law, 次子之子承重與否 … 長孫無子而有弟叔父不當攝祀
items.quote: 今長孫生子，則理當還使主宗 — Now that the eldest grandson has a son, it is proper to return the main lineage to him.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the First Commandment (Exod 20:3-5).
items.needs_role: acting head = second grandson; lineage heir = son of the disabled eldest grandson

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷四 · 居家雜儀下 · 居家雜儀下 · 親屬

items.text: Yield to one another in rank and address, each deferring to the other.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 蓋相推讓之意耳

items.text: When wives of brothers sit together, let the one whose husband is older take the higher seat; do not order by your own age.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 坐以夫之齒

items.text: Call your mother's sisters by a name that honors them as mothers, not as mere aunts.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 從母有母名...降尊以就卑，非禮也。

items.text: In letters to your wife's parents, address them as '外舅' and sign yourself '甥'.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 今依禮經，書以外舅，自稱曰甥，如何？答：似可。

items.text: Do not take precedence over an older brother-in-law by appealing to your wife's age; sit by your own age.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 尹公之父，安得挾妻年，居長我之叔獻上乎？

items.text: Do not treat distant relatives of other surnames as strangers; maintain the affection due to kinsmen.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 曾高外屬，均之路人，簡薄之懷，不亦甚乎？...崇親之義，不宜有限。

items.text: Address an older kinsman of the same surname as '伯父' or '叔父'; if of a different surname, call him '伯舅' or '叔舅'.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 同姓大國曰伯父，小國曰叔父，呼異姓大國曰伯舅，小國曰叔舅

items.text: When addressing an elder of a different surname, use a proper title such as '某姓第幾叔若兄' or '某姓姑夫'; never call him by his personal name.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 未嘗敢呼字也

items.text: Before your own elders call yourself '兒'; before your husband's elders call yourself '新婦'; do not use your given name.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 婦人自稱於己之尊長，則曰『兒』...於夫黨尊長，則曰『新婦』

items.text: Do not speak the personal name of a departed kinsman; treat his name as taboo.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 周人以諱事神，名終將諱之

items.text: If your father is dead, do not change your own name.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 君子已孤，不更名

items.text: Before your parents, refer to yourself by your given name, not as 'I'.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下, 親屬
items.quote: 子於父母則自名...以稱我爲非矣

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷四 · 居家雜儀下 · 居家雜儀下 · 族會

items.text: Attend the ancestral offering whenever the clan holds a rite.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Juhui
items.quote: 宗室有事，族人皆侍奠 — When the ancestral temple has a rite, all clan members attend the offering.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the first commandment: worship belongs to God alone, not ancestors.

items.text: After the ancestral rite, stay for the family feast and drink with joy but with virtue, not to excess.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Juhui
items.quote: 不醉而出，是不親也，醉而不出，是媟宗也 — To leave without drinking is not affectionate; to drink and not leave is disrespectful to the clan.

items.text: Convene a monthly meeting of the whole clan to keep kinship close.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Juhui
items.quote: 凡人家法，須月爲一會，以合族 — Every family's rule: you must have a monthly gathering to unite the clan.

items.text: Hold a gathering also when distant kin come to visit.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Juhui
items.quote: 每有族人遠來，則亦一爲之 — Whenever clan members come from afar, also hold one.

items.text: Exchange proper rites at each other's weddings, funerals, and other significant occasions.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Juhui
items.quote: 吉凶嫁娶之類，更須相與爲禮 — For auspicious and ominous events, weddings and marriages, you must also perform rites for one another.

items.text: Visit each other regularly.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Juhui
items.quote: 其歲月必相往來 — In years and months, they must visit each other.

items.text: Congratulate on happy occasions and condole on sad ones.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Juhui
items.quote: 吉凶必相慶弔 — On auspicious and ominous occasions, they must congratulate and condole.

items.text: See off and welcome each other when traveling.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Juhui
items.quote: 出入必相餞勞 — When going out or coming in, they must see off and welcome.

items.text: Aid and relieve each other in calamity.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Juhui
items.quote: 禍患必相賙恤 — In disasters, they must aid and relieve.

items.text: Meet twice a year at the agreed place, share food, and converse about filial piety, fraternal respect, and each other's welfare, avoiding vulgar topics.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, Juhui
items.quote: 約以歲正月之十日，六月二十日，會于天寧之浮屠...以孝悌忠信相問勞 — Agreed to meet on the tenth of the first month and twentieth of the sixth month at Tianning temple... ask after each other with filial piety, fraternal respect, loyalty, and faithfulness.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷四 · 居家雜儀下 · 居家雜儀下 · 飮食之節

items.text: Taste all food and drink yourself before presenting it to your father, to ensure it is safe and suitable.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 飮食之節
items.quote: 子之於父，飮食必先品嘗之，而後敢進 — A child toward his father: in food and drink he must first taste them and then dare to offer them.

items.text: When attending a superior at a meal, eat a little first as if to test the food, and stop eating only after he stops, to encourage him and show deference.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 飮食之節
items.quote: 侍食於君子，則先飯而後已 — When serving food to a superior, eat first and stop after him.

items.text: Before eating, take a small portion of each dish and set it aside as an offering to the ancestors who first made such food, and do it reverently.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 飮食之節
items.quote: 雖疏食菜羹，必祭，必齊如也 — Even with simple food and vegetable soup, he must offer sacrifice, and must do so with reverence.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead as if they can receive them conflict with the first commandment and biblical teaching that the dead do not eat or hear.

items.text: After an ancestral sacrifice, distribute the sacrificial meat to kinsmen within three days, not letting it remain longer than that.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 飮食之節
items.quote: 家之祭肉，則不出三日，皆以分賜 — The sacrificial meat of the household must not be kept beyond three days; all of it should be distributed.
items.conflict: Sharing food consecrated to ancestors joins in honoring the dead, which conflicts with worshiping God alone.

items.text: When receiving sacrificial meat from an ancestral offering, dress in formal clothes and bow twice to receive it as an act of reverence to the ancestors.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀下 飮食之節
items.quote: 受膰之儀，主人具上服，置膰於案上，再拜而受之禮也 — In the ceremony of receiving sacrificial meat, the host wears formal clothes, places the meat on a table, and bows twice to receive it.
items.conflict: Bowing before food consecrated to ancestors honors the dead, which conflicts with the biblical command to worship God alone.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷四 · 居家雜儀下 · 居家雜儀下 · 書式 … 同居

items.text: Write to elders with proper respect: use honorific titles, ask after their health, and include a word of peace.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 書式
items.quote: 伏惟某位尊體起居萬福，平安字不可闕

items.text: Serve one another as father and son, with mutual deference and care.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 同居
items.quote: 昆季相事，有如父子

items.text: Do not eat delicacies alone; gather with the family and share the meal.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 同居
items.quote: 有美味，不集不食

items.text: Practice forbearance: if shares are unequal or manners imperfect, bear it patiently rather than quarrel.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 同居
items.quote: 能相與忍之，則家道雍睦矣

items.text: Obey the household head in all family affairs and carry out the work he assigns.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 同居
items.quote: 一家之事，聽命焉；歲選子弟，分任家事

items.text: Follow the household head to the ancestral shrine each morning and join in the rites.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 同居
items.quote: 晨興，家長率衆子弟，謁先廟
items.conflict: praying to the dead; Deut 18:10-12

items.text: Rebuke and teach a child who errs; if he does not change, use discipline, and if still stubborn, expel him.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 同居
items.quote: 子弟有過，家長會衆子弟，責而訓之，不改則撻之，終不改度則屛之

items.text: Do your needlework and put all finished goods in the common store; keep nothing in your own room.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 同居
items.quote: 日使諸女諸婦，各一室爲女紅，紅畢斂貯一庫，室無私藏

items.text: Nurse and care for any child who cries; if a mother is away, feed her child as your own.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 同居
items.quote: 幼兒啼泣，諸母見者，卽抱哺；衆婦共乳，不問孰爲己兒

items.text: Uphold the family law and do not let women's words sway you.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 同居
items.quote: 守家法，不聽婦人言而已
items.conflict: Eph 5:21; 1 Pet 3:7; mutual submission; honor wife as co-heir

items.text: Share wealth: give surplus to the lineage heir, and if in want, receive from him.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 異宮同財
items.quote: 異居而同財，有餘則歸之宗，不足則資之宗

items.text: Wait for your parents to finish eating before you eat.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 異宮同財
items.quote: 須待父母食畢，然後可退而食

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷三 · 居家雜儀上 · 居家雜儀上 總

items.text: Assign each member a duty and tasks, and hold them to the success of their work.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 凡爲家長，必謹守禮法，以御羣子弟及家衆，分之以職，授之以事，而責其成功。 — The household head must strictly observe rites and law, assign each younger member and household a duty, entrust them with tasks, and require their success.

items.text: Regulate household expenses by measuring income against outlay; provide food, clothing, and ritual expenses for all according to the family's means, without favoritism, and keep a surplus.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 制財用之節，量入以爲出，稱家之有無，以給上下之衣食 — Regulate expenses by income, measure the household's resources, and provide food and clothing for all.

items.text: In all matters, small or great, do not act on your own; ask the household head for permission.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 凡諸卑幼，事無大小，毋得專行，必咨稟於家長。 — All inferiors: in matters small or great, do not act independently; always ask the household head.
items.conflict: Adult sons need not seek parental permission for every act; Gen 2:24, Eph 6:1.

items.text: Do not keep private wealth: hand over your salary and income from fields and houses to your parents, and ask before using or lending.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 毋得蓄私財。俸祿及田宅所入，盡歸之父母舅姑 — Do not keep private wealth; salaries and income from fields and houses all go to parents and parents-in-law.
items.conflict: Adult sons should support own household; common purse not required, 1 Tim 5:8.

items.text: Do not keep private goods or savings; hand over all gifts you receive to your parents-in-law, and do not lend or give without their leave.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 子婦無私貨，無私蓄，無私器。不敢私假，不敢私與。 — Sons and daughters-in-law have no private goods, savings, or utensils; they dare not privately lend or give.
items.conflict: Wife's primary loyalty to husband, own household economy, Gen 2:24.

items.text: Serve your uncle's wife as you would your own mother; bring all family affairs to her for decision, and give your earnings to her for distribution.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 家事巨細，一以咨決。每兄弟出行有獲，則尺寸以上，皆入李之庫 — In all family matters, consult her; whatever the brothers gained, even a foot or inch, went into Aunt Li's storehouse.
items.conflict: Total submission of earnings to aunt beyond biblical requirement, 1 Tim 5:16.

items.text: Rise before dawn, wash, dress, and go to your parents' room to ask after their health; at night, see them to bed and bid them good night.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 天欲明，咸起盥漱櫛總具冠帶。昧爽，適父母舅姑之所，省問。 — At dawn, rise, wash, comb, dress, and go to your parents'/in-laws' place to ask after their health.

items.text: When your parents rise, personally bring their medicine and prepare their morning meal; do not leave these tasks to servants.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 父母舅姑起，子供藥物，婦具晨羞。 — When parents and in-laws rise, sons bring medicine, daughters-in-law prepare the morning meal.

items.text: Do not begin eating before your elders have lifted their chopsticks; then go to your own place to eat.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 尊長舉筯，子婦乃各退就食。 — When elders lift their chopsticks, children and daughters-in-law then go to eat.

items.text: In your parents' presence, be reverent in appearance and careful in service; speak softly, do not sit or leave without their command.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 父母舅姑，不命之坐，不敢坐，不命之退，不敢退。 — Without parents'/in-laws' order to sit, do not sit; without order to leave, do not leave.

items.text: Write down your parents' instructions, carry them out promptly, and report back; if you think a command is wrong, explain your reasons gently, but if they insist, comply.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 凡子受父母之命，必籍記而佩之，時省而速行之，事畢則返命焉。 — When a son receives his parents' commands, write them down, carry them out promptly, and report back when done.
items.conflict: Obedience for children, not adults; conscience before parents if they command sin, Eph 6:1, Acts 5:29.

items.text: If your parent is wrong, remonstrate with a gentle manner and soft voice; if they are displeased, remain respectful and try again when they are receptive; do not hold resentment.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 凡父母有過，下氣怡色，柔聲以諫。諫若不入，起敬起孝，悅則復諫。 — If your parents err, remonstrate with gentle voice and pleasant face; if not accepted, remain respectful and try again when they are pleased.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷三 · 居家雜儀上 · 居家雜儀上 總

items.text: When your mother is in error, correct her gently and by yielding, not harshly, lest you wound affection and fail to reach her.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 子之於母，當以柔巽補導之 — A son toward his mother should use gentleness to guide her.

items.text: Remonstrate with your parents when they do wrong; if after three attempts they do not listen, follow them weeping.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 三諫而不聽，則號泣而隨之 — Remonstrate three times; if not heeded, wail and follow.

items.text: Do not let wealth or rank make you presume above your father, elder brother, or clan.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 不敢以貴富，加於父兄宗族 — Do not use wealth or rank to override father, elder brother, or clan.

items.text: Serve the lineage heir and his wife with respect; do not bring your wealth or rank into his house.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 雖貴富，不敢以貴富，入宗子之家 — Though rich, do not bring wealth into the lineage heir's house.

items.text: Though you hold high office, do not be arrogant before your elder brother; dismount and walk.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 下車步入 — Dismount and walk.

items.text: When you go out, tell your parents; when you return, show yourself; do not take your father's place or privileges.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 出必告，反必面 — When going out, tell; when returning, present yourself.

items.text: When they are ill, stay by them and personally prepare and taste their medicine.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 親調嘗藥餌而供之 — Personally prepare and taste their medicine and offer it.

items.text: While your parent is ill, restrain your pleasures: do not groom yourself, play music, or feast; return to normal when they recover.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 父母有疾，琴瑟不御 — When parents are ill, do not play instruments.

items.text: Love and honor what your parents love and honor, even their dogs and horses.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 父母所愛，亦當愛之 — What parents love, you also love.

items.text: If your daughter-in-law is not filial, teach her patiently; if she does not mend, scold and beat her; if she still does not, send her away.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 屢笞而終不改，子放婦出 — If after repeated beating she does not change, the son may put away the wife.
items.conflict: A husband must love his wife; physical abuse is sin; marriage is indissoluble except for adultery.

items.text: If your parents are displeased with your wife, divorce her; if they say she serves them well, keep her all your life.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 子甚宜其妻，父母不悅，出 — If the son loves his wife but parents dislike her, put her away.
items.conflict: A man shall leave father and mother and cleave to his wife; parents may not dissolve marriage.

items.text: When your parent is gravely ill, pray to the Northern Dipper that you may die in their place.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 居家雜儀上 總
items.quote: 每稽顙北辰，求以身代 — Each evening he bowed to the Northern Dipper, asking to die in his father's place.
items.conflict: Prayer to any but God alone is idolatry; only Christ is our substitute.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷一 · 宗法 · 宗法 · 出後子以其庶子還承其父 … 取孫行爲後

items.text: Adopt an heir from the same clan and only from your son's generation; never adopt a grandchild, brother, or superior, for that would disorder the ancestral line.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 出後子以其庶子還承其父 … 取孫行爲後
items.quote: 立後者，不得尊卑失序，以亂宗族。尊屬與兄弟及孫，不相爲後。 — When appointing an heir, do not disturb the order of superior and inferior and disorder the clan; do not make a superior, brother, or grandson one's heir.

items.text: Treat the adoptive father as your own father; carry on the ancestral rites and continue the lineage.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 出後子以其庶子還承其父 … 取孫行爲後
items.quote: 禮，爲人後者，爲之子...承先祀而繼統緖 — When one becomes another's heir, he becomes his son... can carry on ancestral rites and continue the line.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration is forbidden by the Second Commandment; worship belongs to God alone.

items.text: If your biological parents have no heir and both fathers agree, return to continue their line; if they are dead, do not cancel the adoption but include them as attached tablets.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 出後子以其庶子還承其父 … 取孫行爲後
items.quote: 出後者，本生親無後，則兩家父相議，歸宗...兩家父死，則子不可擅自罷繼，當以本生親，爲班祔也。 — If birth parents have no heir, the two fathers deliberate and he returns; if fathers dead, he may not cancel but make them attached tablets.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration is forbidden by the Second Commandment; worship belongs to God alone.
items.needs_role: child adopted out to another family (出後)

items.text: Once an heir is adopted, do not deprive him of his position or demote him, even if the adoption was irregular; uphold the established lineage.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 出後子以其庶子還承其父 … 取孫行爲後
items.quote: 今永陽，取興寧爲後，則興寧，是嫡孫也，而可奪其宗乎？...今欲貶抑長嗣，爲別宗，則名義不正 — Can you rob him of his lineage? ... to demote the eldest heir and make him a separate lineage, the name and position would not be right.

items.text: When the elder brother's widow adopts an heir, yield the ancestral rites to that heir and do not hold on to the office.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 出後子以其庶子還承其父 … 取孫行爲後
items.quote: 次子之子曰，『伯父早歿，祖父，雖以家君奉祀，而今伯母立後，則當奉祀。』...告廟還宗，終似得禮。 — The second son's son said, 'Now that my aunt has adopted an heir, he should perform the rites.' ... Report to the temple and return the lineage.
items.needs_role: second son's son acting as heir

items.text: As the family elder, oversee disputes over succession: report the whole matter to the temple and restore the proper heir.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 出後子以其庶子還承其父 … 取孫行爲後
items.quote: 然則今日之義，乃是門長事也，具其本末，告廟還宗，終似得禮。 — The right course is the family elder's affair: lay out the whole matter, report to the temple, and restore the lineage.

items.text: Do not seek to overturn the succession your ancestors arranged; instead offer your filial reverence in the rites as best you can.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 出後子以其庶子還承其父 … 取孫行爲後
items.quote: 不有其祖先區處而追欲移宗者，其失可知矣。 — To disregard the ancestors' arrangement and later seek to shift the lineage—the error is evident.

items.text: When the lineage heir has died, you who act in his place must not take his title 'filial'; call yourself by name only.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 宗法 出後子以其庶子還承其父 … 取孫行爲後
items.quote: 宗子，死，稱名，不言孝，身歿而已。註：孝，宗子之稱，不敢與之同。 — When the lineage heir dies, name yourself; do not say 'filial' — 'filial' is the lineage heir's title; do not share it.

work: Sangbyeon Tonggo, General Rites: ancestral shrine, unmoved tablets, lineage law
heading: 常變通攷 卷一 · 宗法 · 宗法 · 養異姓子爲後 … 外孫奉祀

items.text: Do not adopt a child of a different surname as your heir, for that would confuse the lineage and cut off the ancestral worship.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 不得養異姓爲後，以亂宗族 — Do not adopt a different surname as heir, so as to disturb the clan.
items.conflict: Adoption for ancestor worship; God forbids ancestor rites (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: If you have no son, adopt a boy from your own clan to continue the line and its sacrifices, not a stranger's child.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 大宗無子，則以族人之子續之 — If the great lineage has no son, take a son from the clan to continue it.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is forbidden; motive of continuing sacrifices is not biblical.

items.text: Repay your foster parents with all your strength for the kindness of raising you from certain death.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 竭其筋力，報於公嫗育養之澤 — Exhaust your strength to repay the kindness of your foster parents' nurture.

items.text: Do not abandon your birth parents or turn against the kindness of having given you life; repay their gift of life with mourning at their death.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 不得出所生，而背恩情。報生以死 — Do not leave your birth parents and betray kindness; repay life with death.

items.text: If both your adoptive and birth families lack heirs, when you have a son, set him up as heir to your birth father, and until then offer sacrifices in a separate room.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 有子，以後其父，未有後之間，別立室以祭祀 — When you have a son, make him heir to your own father; until then set up a separate room for sacrifice.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is forbidden (Deut 18:10-12; 1 Cor 10:20).

items.text: If your adoptive father has his own heir and your birth line is extinct, return to your original surname and continue that line's sacrifices.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 所養之父，自有後，而本絶祀者，便當還宗 — If the adoptive father has his own heir and the birth line is extinct, return to your original lineage.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is forbidden (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: On New Year, Dano, Mid-autumn, and their death anniversaries, offer customary rites to your maternal grandparents if they have no other heir to do so.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 當於正朝端午仲秋及各忌日，用俗儀祭之 — On New Year, Dano, Mid-autumn and death anniversaries, use customary rites to sacrifice.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is forbidden (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: If you keep the spirit tablets of your maternal ancestors because their line has no heir, place them in a separate shrine, not in your clan shrine, and visit them there.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 權宜奉置別所，往來展省 — Provisionally place them in a separate place and go back and forth to tend them.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is forbidden (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Worship one generation fewer for your external ancestors than you do for your own clan.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 本宗，祭四代，則外家祀，當減一代 — If the main line worships four generations, external family worship should reduce by one generation.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is forbidden (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Do not sacrifice to the ancestors of a different lineage, for spirits do not accept offerings from those not of their kind.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 神不歆非類，民不祀非族 — Spirits do not accept offerings from those not of their kind; people do not sacrifice to those not of their lineage.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is forbidden (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: When ancestral rites are led by a non-agnatic adopted heir, participate with wholehearted filial reverence, not leaving the sacrifice to him alone.
items.citation: Sangbyeon Tonggo, 卷一·宗法·宗法·養異姓子爲後…外孫奉祀
items.quote: 預祭之時，盡吾孝敬之誠心，可也 — At the time of the sacrifice, exhaust your filial reverence and sincere heart, that is all.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is forbidden (Deut 18:10-12).
